version_note: git main (crytic org, formerly published under trailofbits/solana-lints; crytic is Trail of Bits' blockchain-security org), dylint-based lint library, pinned to rust-toolchain nightly-2025-01-09 with llvm-tools-preview and rustc-dev components. Installed and run in a rust:slim container via cargo-dylint + dylint-link, nothing on the host.
derivation: Mapping derived from the library's OWN README table (7 lints, each row naming the sealevel-attacks class it targets by name and linking to that class's page in coral-xyz/sealevel-attacks), fetched and read BEFORE any corpus run. Not derived from which lints happened to fire.
right_of_reply: Not sent to Trail of Bits / Crytic. Under PROTOCOL.md this mapping should be offered to the tool's authors for correction before the result is treated as final, and their correction published.
in_sample_warning: solana-lints was built explicitly against coral-xyz/sealevel-attacks: its own README links each lint directly to the matching class page in that corpus, and the project describes itself as inspired by the Sealevel Attacks. Any score on corpus 1 should be read as in-sample, the same caveat as Radar and X-Ray.
unmapped_note: All 7 of solana-lints' lints map to a corpus-1 class; none are excluded as noise-only. sysvar_get is a narrower rule than the corpus's own framing of class 10 (it flags Sysvar::from_account_info instead of Sysvar::get specifically, rather than address validation in general), mapped here because it is the lint the project itself links to the sysvar-address-checking class page.
structural_gaps: Four classes have no solana-lints rule at all: 1-account-data-matching, 4-initialization, 6-duplicate-mutable-accounts, 8-pda-sharing. These count as misses for a reason that has nothing to do with detection quality on the 7 classes the library does target.
installability_note: See report body for the exact outcome. If the tool could not be made to run in the time budgeted, this file records the pre-registered mapping anyway per PROTOCOL.md's own standard: intent and mapping do not depend on whether the run succeeded.
